7783.stem: A bag contains 11 red lollies and 5 blue lollies. Sarah takes a lolly from the bag without looking and eats it. She then takes another without looking and eats it.

figures.cap: solution sketch: hand-drawn tree diagram with branch probabilities

parts.latex: What is the probability Sarah will choose a blue lolly for her first choice?
By drawing a tree diagram, find the probability that Sarah eats two lollies of different colours.

solutions.latex:
There are $5$ blue lollies among $16$ in total.
$$P(B) = \dfrac{5}{16}$$

\exfigure{708_q19_s1}

The lollies are eaten, so the second pick is without replacement. Different colours means $RB$ or $BR$.
$$\begin{aligned} P(RB) &= \dfrac{11}{16} \times \dfrac{5}{15} = \dfrac{11}{48} \\ P(BR) &= \dfrac{5}{16} \times \dfrac{11}{15} = \dfrac{11}{48} \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} P(BR \text{ or } RB) &= \dfrac{11}{48} + \dfrac{11}{48} \\ &= \dfrac{11}{24} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ P(\text{different colours}) = \dfrac{11}{24}$$
criteria: Draws the tree diagram and finds the probabilities of $RB$ and $BR$, or equivalent merit
Draws the tree diagram, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Source rubric was '1 for tree diagram; 1 for calculation; 1 for answer'; rewritten top-down.

7933.stem: Three men and five women are competing in the latest episode of survivor.

figures.cap: blank two-stage tree diagram, Male/Female at each selection
solution sketch: tree diagram completed with probabilities

parts.latex: If one person is selected at random, what is the probability that this person is female?
What is the probability that $1$ female and $1$ male were eliminated from the island?

criteria: Completes some of the branch probabilities, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
One male and one female can be eliminated in two orders, each with probability $\dfrac{15}{56}$.
$$\begin{aligned} P(\text{male and female}) &= \dfrac{15}{56}+\dfrac{15}{56} \\ &= \dfrac{30}{56} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds one correct branch probability, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us. $\dfrac{30}{56}$ left unsimplified as in source.
